api.notes: Returns a template, a node or text (never HTML). Called for the collapsed items and, hidden, for all items (the widest indicator is measured from that copy).
Non-cancelable notification; `items` carries each collapsed element and its original index. Silent while nothing overflows, including on mount (OVERFLOW-03).
The spacing step names the --spacing-* token (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10).
observeSelf and observeParent are kebab-case: observe-self, observe-parent.

api.reason: A-xstyle: use class/style, ::part(overflow-list) and the gap attribute.

hooks.notes: @tecton-wc/core/controllers/overflow.js: the reactive wrapper; `computeOverflow` is the pure fit computation (upstream tests ported to overflow.node.test.ts).

differences.text: Items are the host's light-DOM children, measured in place (every item is revealed, read and re-hidden in one synchronous pass, so nothing flickers) instead of a hidden inert clone of all children: light-DOM nodes cannot be rendered in two places. Collapsed children get data-tct-overflow and are hidden with display: none, so they stay in the DOM but leave the tab order and the accessibility tree. Items are natural width (flex: none). Only the indicator is measured from a hidden inert copy, rendered for all items.

An indicator is drawn only when `overflowRenderer` is set (as upstream), or when the additive `show-count` attribute asks for the built-in "+N" chip, named "N more" through the new message @tct.overflow-list.overflow. `overflowRenderer` returns a template, a node or text rather than a ReactNode; OverflowItem is {element, index} (upstream {child, index}).

`onOverflowChange` is the non-cancelable notification event tct-overflow-change. Its reports are keyed on the collapsed items' indices and element identities (upstream: indices and React keys), so a membership or order change with the same count reports and an unrelated re-render does not; there is no separate callback identity to worry about.

The gap is read from the computed column gap of the row (the spacing token) rather than a px table, so a theme that retunes the spacing scale stays measured correctly. `behavior` values are kebab-case.
The row clips with `overflow: clip` and a clip margin of one focus-ring width plus offset (falling back to `hidden`), so a focus ring on an edge item is not cut off.

requests.reason: The rule flags every `new Tct*()`, including the library event classes (`new TctOverflowChangeEvent(...)`, which A§7.6 requires), so this element imports them under an alias. Exclude class names ending in `Event`.

'English namespace modules > partition the English catalog by namespace' compares the merged dist/en modules to the upstream English catalog, so any first-party @tct.* message fails it (@tct.overflow-list.overflow here, and @tct.field.* from WP-F). Compare only the @tct.* ids, and assert the @tct.* ids sit in the module named after their namespace.

core.overflow-list.notes: Guides: [mwg:size-aware-styling] and [mwg:css-layout] responsive by measuring the space given, not the viewport; [mwg:overflow-clipping-control] clip with a margin so focus rings survive; [mwg:accessible-web-components] hidden items leave the tree; [mwg:shadow-dom] slots and slotchange re-measure. The measurement is a single synchronous reveal-read-restore pass to avoid flicker.
